summary: There are independent cap-one compact finite-fragment X,X' and cap-one L~Unif[epsilon,epsilon+1] such that for Y=-2LX' every unnormalised L=l slice obeys mu_l(I)<=|I|^(1/2) for every interval I, uniformly with constant 1, yet T=2LX+Y=2L(X-X') has p_T(0)=(1/2)log((1+epsilon)/epsilon), which diverges as epsilon->0. Thus interval-only square-root Frostman control cannot by itself feed an arbitrary rough-hub L-infinity receiver. The quadratic matrix has spectrum {sqrt(2),-sqrt(2),0}, so this is not a counterexample to the three-large-eigenvalue conjecture. The account04/B14 r9 interval/Fourier slice bounds remain valid; only the interval-only rough-hub endpoint is refuted as an abstract inference.

partner_control.application: For the same fragmented laws, 2U1U2+(1/2)(X+X'-beta)^2 has three large eigenvalues and density <=4+2log(8)<8.159 uniformly.
